Subject: Re: MAP draft & acceptance window — ask to re-anchor

Marissa —

Thanks again for the detailed MAP draft. Procurement had an emergency vendor review this morning and they need an extra two weeks before they can sign the final SOW. That pushes our internal test schedule out and would make the current acceptance window (12/15 — 12/22) unrealistic.

We want to avoid slipping the go-live by more than two weeks. Can you propose a re-anchored MAP that keeps the public launch target but staggers acceptance activities (canary -> phased traffic -> final signoff)? I attached our updated acceptance checklist (Medivale_proposed_acceptance_v2.pdf) with the procurement note highlighted.

We also expect procurement to request a credit/penalty clause if the timeline changes; want to surface that now so we can include it in the mutual action plan.

Appreciate a quick read — Tom and procurement are on standby for a call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Director, Platform Programs | Medivale Health

Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft & acceptance window — ask to re-anchor

Sarah — thanks for the heads up and for the attachment. I’m sorry procurement hit the vendor review; we’ll be flexible here.

Initial reaction / proposal from Redwood:  
- Option A (staggered anchors, low-risk): keep public launch date, move final acceptance window to 01/05-01/12, introduce a two-stage acceptance path: (1) 12/20-12/24 canary (1% traffic, functional smoke), (2) 12/27-01/04 phased traffic ramp (10% -> 50%), (3) 01/05 final acceptance.
- Option B (conservative): push final acceptance and go-live two weeks, with a tightened canary earlier for readiness gating.

We can absorb a one-week slippage without credits; beyond that we should discuss a modest credit/extension framework. I’ve looped Ben (SE) for the canary ops plan and Camila (CS) for the acceptance checklist alignment. Rishi — please advise on the contract language draft for a credit/extension clause.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick sync (30m) this week to choose Option A vs B — please propose windows.
2) If Option A: Ben to share a minimal canary runbook and rollback triggers (I attached redwood_canary_plan.pdf).
3) Rishi to draft a short mutual-action addendum capturing the acceptance re-anchor and credit guardrails.
4) We’ll update MAP_reanchor_matrix.xlsx and share a single source of truth in Drive.

I’ll wait for Tom or procurement to propose a time; otherwise I can send 3 slots tomorrow.

—Marissa

Marissa / Sarah —

I reviewed Medivale_proposed_acceptance_v2 and mapped it against our canary controls. Quick notes:
- Canary at 1% traffic is fine for feature validation; include an explicit KV-cache-warmup window (12–24 hours) before traffic begins.
- Rollback triggers: >5% error rate sustained for 10m OR two consecutive critical P0 alerts = immediate rollback.
- Data migration validation: we need a short dry-run in a staging slice; 11/28–11/30 looks good on our side.

I attached a trimmed runbook (redwood_canary_plan.pdf) with the exact metric thresholds we’ll use. If procurement still expects credit language, we should include operational gates (canary intact & migration validated) as exceptions to credit triggers.

I can be on the call if you want to walk the metrics live.

—Ben

Subject: Fwd: MAP draft & acceptance window — re-anchor proposal + escalation ladder

Team — forwarding the thread to capture an escalation ladder and a final contingency ask. TL;DR: procurement delay at Medivale may push final acceptance; customer prefers to keep public launch date and stagger acceptance. Recommended internal course: accept Option A (staggered anchors) with the following commercial guardrails:

Escalation ladder & commercial contingency (proposed):
1) Internal: AE (Rishi) + SE (Ben) to confirm ops gates (canary metrics & migration dry-run). If gates pass, no credit applies.
2) If gates fail and remediation extends timeline by <= 7 calendar days, Redwood absorbs impact (no credit).
3) If remediation extends timeline by > 7 and <= 21 calendar days, offer a one-time credit of 5% of first-month committed usage or equivalent professional-services hours.
4) If delay > 21 days, exec review and structured credit/extended billing pause to be negotiated.

Operational contingency: Ben to run dry-run 11/28–11/30; canary 12/20–12/24 (1% traffic) with rollback triggers defined. Camila will hold the acceptance checklist alignment and sign-off playbook. Rishi to draft the short addendum and circulate to procurement.

I’ve attached the MAP_reanchor_matrix.xlsx (living doc) and the current canary runbook. Please reply with any objections by EOD tomorrow so I can present a single recommended position on the call with Medivale. If no objections, I’ll put the addendum draft in Drive and propose the three call slots to Medivale.

Thanks —
Marissa
